subject: Access to admin logs for SOC 2: escrow and on-demand pulls
messages:
From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@healthbridge.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: DataSec Team <security@healthbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: admin activity logs for SOC 2 — escrow and on-demand pulls

Hi Jasmine,

We're preparing for our SOC 2 Type II evidence collection and need clarity on Redwood's admin activity logging and export capabilities. Specifically HealthBridge needs:

- A short inventory of what admin/operator events are recorded (e.g., UI sign-ins, API key ops, role changes, policy edits, console actions, session metadata, KV cache invalidation events).
- Default retention and whether retention is configurable per account/tenant.
- Export options: scheduled snapshots vs on-demand pulls, accepted formats, manifest and checksum approaches, and chain-of-custody evidence.
- Ability to escrow copies (HealthBridge requires a copy of admin logs to be deposited with an escrow provider for 7-year retention in a signed, attestable bundle).

Could you provide a short written response and an example manifest/checksum approach? Also let us know the lead time for an on-demand export (SLA) and whether you can sign attestation of the export integrity (HMAC/PKI).

Thanks — we can loop in legal if needed but wanted to start with the technical specifics.

—Morgan
Morgan Lee
Data Security Manager, HealthBridge
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@healthbridge.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity logs for SOC 2 — escrow and on-demand pulls

Morgan — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise inventory plus export options. Attaching a draft manifest (log_manifest_draft_v1.pdf) and a sample checksum file for reference.

What we log (high level):
- Authentication events: successful/failed admin console logins, MFA challenges, SSO assertions (SAML/OIDC).
- Authorization changes: role grants/revokes, policy edits, permission changes.
- API key lifecycle: creation, rotation, disablement, deletion.
- Console and API actions: create/update/delete operations on resources (models, deployments, routes), configuration changes, rollout actions.
- Privileged operations: key exports, KMS/HSM calls (we log the call, not the secret material).
- Operational telemetry: session IDs, source IP, user agent, request id, latency bucket.
- KV/cache events: cache invalidations and miss/hit metrics (included on request — more on this below).

Retention and configuration:
- Default retention: 365 days for admin activity and audit traces.
- Configurable: enterprise customers can request extended retention windows (30 days up to 7 years) as part of a Dedicated or Private deployment contract; this is enforced at the bucket/manifest level and documented in the export.

Export modes and formats:
- Scheduled snapshots: daily compressed JSONL bundles (each line = JSON event, RFC3339 timestamps) with an attested manifest.
- On-demand pulls: ad-hoc ZIP containing: events.jsonl (or events.parquet on request), manifest.json, checksums.txt (SHA256), and a signed attestation (HMAC-SHA256 or x.509 signature). Typical turnaround: 24–72 hours depending on scope and sampling.
- Delivery: S3 presigned URL (PUT or GET), SFTP transfer, or secure HTTPS download behind an expiring token.
- Chain-of-custody: manifest includes export start/end times, export operator, digest per file, and a server-side signature. We can provide a signed HMAC (customer-shared secret) or an x.509-signed manifest for legal/escrow needs.

Escrow and long-term retention:
- We can produce an escrow-ready bundle (signed manifest + checksums + compression) for third-party deposition. For Hosted customers, escrow is supported via an enterprise add-on (we create the bundle and upload to an escrow provider or to a customer-designated S3 bucket).
- For Private/Dedicated customers with retention >1 year we can also provide retention-preserved storage (locked lifecycle policies) and periodic attestations.

PII/redaction and sampling:
- By default events include identifying metadata (user id/email, source IP truncated to /24 when requested). PII redaction or pseudonymization is available for exports if required by contract.
- We can provide full exports or sampled windows; sampling criteria are timestamp ranges and event-types.

Next steps / proposed actions:
- If this aligns, we can schedule a 30-minute technical call to finalize manifest fields and retention SLA.
- I've attached a draft manifest and a sample checksum for you to review.

Action items:
1) Morgan: confirm desired retention window for escrow (7 years requested) and preferred delivery method.
2) Ben/Grace: propose a timeline and estimate for creating the escrow bundle and associated pricing for storage/attestation.
3) Olga: prepare a short attestation template we can sign that covers export integrity and chain-of-custody language.

Happy to hop on a call — my calendar link is in the signature.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@healthbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity logs for SOC 2 — escrow and on-demand pulls

On Wed, Jul 30, 2025 at 11:03 AM jasmine_liu@redwood.ai wrote:
> Morgan — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise inventory plus export options....

Adding technical details from the runtime/export side:

- Format specifics: events.jsonl (newline-delimited JSON) with these top-level fields: event_id, timestamp (RFC3339 UTC), tenant_id, user_id, actor_role, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, client_ip (masked if requested), metadata (free-form). We can also provide Parquet exports for high-volume deliveries.
- Sequencing: exports include a contiguous sequence_id and export_window_start/end so you can verify completeness.
- Checksums: SHA256 per file + an overall manifest digest (we recommend signing the manifest with our platform key).
- KV/cache events: by default we record cache invalidations and metadata (cache_key hashed, event type). We do not include full payloads by default; can include hashed/not-plain keys on request — this is common for customers wanting full traceability for debugging vs those needing strict PII limits.
- Timezone/normalization: all exported timestamps are normalized to UTC and include original offset if available.
- Compression & encryption: exports are gzip-compressed; HIPAA/PII-sensitive exports can be additionally encrypted with customer-provided GPG key prior to transfer.

Operational constraints and SLA expectations:
- On-demand export SLA (baseline hosted): 72 hours for up to 30 days of data; 5–10 business days for multi-month/year extracts depending on retention size. Dedicated/Private customers can get expedited windows.
- For escrow deposits we recommend: 1) generate export bundle, 2) compute signed manifest, 3) upload to escrow (S3) with restricted access, 4) provide attested transfer logs (S3 put object events) as proof of handoff.

I'll attach the short export_playbook.md that lists commands and expected outputs for our ops team.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Product — Redwood Inference
From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@healthbridge.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: DataSec Team <security@healthbridge.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity logs for SOC 2 — escrow and on-demand pulls

Thanks, Jasmine and Grace — this is helpful and covers most of our questions. A few follow-ups:

- HealthBridge confirms we want escrow retention of 7 years for admin activity logs. We prefer an escrow deposit to our designated S3 bucket (HealthBridge-escrow) with an x.509-signed manifest.
- Please include legal-hold semantics: ability to freeze/defer deletion for a tenant when requested by our legal team.
- For chain-of-custody we need: (a) signed manifest + per-file SHA256 checksums, (b) S3 PutObject logs (or equivalent) showing the deposit, and (c) attestation signed by a Redwood officer confirming the export contents match live records at time of export.

Proposed next step: schedule a quick call to land on the manifest fields and get a pricing/ops estimate. We are available Tues/Wed next week 10:00–13:00 PT. I'll attach a short SOW request for procurement (HealthBridge_SOW_Request.pdf).

Ben — can you include a ballpark for escrow storage + export fees in the call?

—Morgan

P.S. Ben — we can accept HMAC if x.509 incurs delays, but we prefer the x.509 path if available for legal reasons.
